units.title: Subject–verb agreement
units.intro: The verb must agree with its true subject in number, even when phrases come between them.

cards.title: Basic agreement
rule: Singular subject → singular verb: *The exam **starts** at eight.*
Plural subject → plural verb: *The exams **start** at eight.*
A phrase between subject and verb does not change agreement: *The box of books **is** heavy.*

examples.text: The list of names is long.
The list of names are long.
examples.fix: The list of names is long.

cards.title: Tricky cases
rule: *either … or / neither … nor* → agree with the nearer noun.
Collective nouns may be singular when the group acts as one.

examples.text: Neither the teachers nor the principal was late.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: Ignore prepositional phrases after the subject; agree with the head noun.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Singular subjects take singular verbs; plural subjects take plural verbs; watch collective and either/or.

tips.text: Ignore prepositional phrases after the subject; agree with the head noun.

questions.q: One of the most challenging obstacles facing high school graduates ________ the rising cost of higher education.
questions.label: 1. One of the most challenging obstacles facing high school gra

similar.q: One of the most challenging obstacles facing high
The board of directors, despite having conflicting

why: The subject of the sentence is 'One' (singular) in the pattern $$\text{One of} + \text{Plural Noun} + \text{Singular Verb}$$. The plural noun phrase 'the most challenging obstacles' is part of a prepositional phrase modifying the subject.
Students often match the verb to the plural noun 'obstacles' which is closest to the verb slot, leading them to choose 'are' (Option A). This is a classic attraction trap in matriculation exams.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The board of directors, despite having conflicting opinions on the new expansion policy, ________ finally agreed on the budget.
questions.label: 2. The board of directors, despite having conflicting opinions

similar.q: The board of directors, despite having conflicting
Neither the regional program coordinator nor the s

why: The subject is 'The board' (singular collective noun). The phrase 'of directors' and the parenthetical clause 'despite having conflicting opinions...' are intervening elements that do not change the subject's singular number.

Students are often distracted by the plural nouns 'directors' and 'opinions' and select the plural auxiliary 'have' (Option B). Isolating the subject 'The board' reveals that the singular 'has' is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Neither the regional program coordinator nor the senior researchers ________ present at the emergency project meeting yesterday.
questions.label: 3. Neither the regional program coordinator nor the senior rese

similar.q: Neither the regional program coordinator nor the s
The local police ________ currently searching the

why: The compound subject is connected by the correlative conjunction 'Neither... nor'. The proximity rule applies, meaning the verb agrees with the closer subject, 'the senior researchers' (plural).

Students may focus on 'the coordinator' (singular) and choose 'was' (Option A). The past time marker 'yesterday' eliminates present auxiliaries 'is' and 'are', leaving 'were' (Option B) as the correct choice.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The local police ________ currently searching the forest area for the prisoners who escaped from the regional jail.
questions.label: 4. The local police ________ currently searching the forest are

similar.q: The local police ________ currently searching the
Mathematics ________ always been regarded as a fou

why: 'Police' is a collective noun that is always plural in English and must be paired with plural verbs.

Because 'police' does not end in '-s', students often assume it is singular and choose 'is' (Option A) or 'was' (Option C). The time marker 'currently' indicates present tense, which makes 'are' (Option B) correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Mathematics ________ always been regarded as a foundational subject for engineering students worldwide.
questions.label: 5. Mathematics ________ always been regarded as a foundational

similar.q: Mathematics ________ always been regarded as a fou
Three thousand dollars ________ too much to pay fo

why: Academic subjects ending in '-ics' (mathematics, physics, politics) look plural because of the '-s' suffix, but they are singular uncountable nouns. The perfect auxiliary 'been' requires 'has' or 'have'.
Students are often tricked by the '-s' at the end of 'Mathematics' and select 'have' (Option B). This is a common spelling-appearance trap on ESSLCE exams.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Three thousand dollars ________ too much to pay for a second-hand water pump in this small town.
questions.label: 6. Three thousand dollars ________ too much to pay for a second

similar.q: Three thousand dollars ________ too much to pay fo
One of the most challenging obstacles facing high

why: Nouns representing specific quantities of money, time, distance, or weight are treated as a single, collective unit ($$\text{Quantity} \rightarrow \text{Singular Verb}$$).
Students see the plural noun 'dollars' and choose 'are' (Option A) or 'were' (Option C). However, because the amount is treated as a single sum, it requires the singular verb 'is' (Option B).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Not only the students but also their instructor ________ highly motivated to complete the laboratory project before the semester ends.
questions.label: 7. Not only the students but also their instructor ________ hig

similar.q: One of the most challenging obstacles facing high

why: The compound subject is connected by 'not only... but also'. The verb must agree with the closer subject, which is 'their instructor' (singular).

Students may choose the plural 'are' (Option B) because they see both 'students' and 'instructor' and assume the subject must be plural. The proximity rule requires the singular verb 'is' (Option A) to match the singular 'instructor'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Some of the milk in the larger containers ________ spoiled, so we must discard it immediately.
questions.label: 8. Some of the milk in the larger containers ________ spoiled,

similar.q: The board of directors, despite having conflicting

why: 'Some' belongs to the SANAM variable category. Its grammatical number is determined by the noun in the modifying prepositional phrase: 'of the milk'. Since 'milk' is uncountable (singular), 'Some' is singular.
Students may look at 'containers' (plural) and select a plural verb like 'have' (Option B) or 'are' (Option C). The correct auxiliary is 'has' (Option A) to match the uncountable noun 'milk'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The soccer team ________ currently putting on their individual uniforms in the locker room.
questions.label: 9. The soccer team ________ currently putting on their individu

similar.q: Neither the regional program coordinator nor the s

why: 'Team' is a collective noun. The context 'putting on their individual uniforms' shows that the members are acting as separate individuals, which requires a plural verb.
Students often assume collective nouns are always singular and choose 'is' (Option B). The use of the plural possessive pronoun 'their' confirms that the verb must be plural 'are' (Option A).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Every single book, including the rare historical manuscripts in the library vault, ________ cataloged last year.
questions.label: 10. Every single book, including the rare historical manuscripts

similar.q: The local police ________ currently searching the

why: 'Every single book' is the subject of the sentence. The indefinite modifier 'Every' is singular. The phrase 'including the rare historical manuscripts...' is an intervening phrase that does not affect the subject's singular number.

Students often choose 'were' (Option B) or 'are' (Option C) because they match the verb to the plural 'manuscripts' or 'vault'. The past time marker 'last year' requires the singular past verb 'was' (Option A).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.
